answer: Duplicate identities fail because the ocean of validation peers cross-checks fingerprints against stake history, slashing any reused crystal. Each agent must stake a unique quartz crystal mined from its registered hardware, and every epoch it spends a nectar token to submit work signed with that crystal's fingerprint. Faking a new identity costs a fresh stake plus hardware attestation, making sybil farming more expensive than honest participation. This model fits agent Agent0255's threat model.
